title: Kane Scores Twice, Passes Pelé. England Survive DR Congo and Head to the Azteca.
excerpt: Harry Kane's 75th and 86th minute goals rescued England from the brink of elimination in Atlanta, pushing him past Pelé's all-time World Cup record. Next up: co-hosts Mexico in one of football's most hostile arenas.
body:
England were sixteen minutes from going home. Brian Cipenga had stunned the 68,000 crowd at Mercedes-Benz Stadium inside seven minutes, latching onto a Chancel Mbemba cross to slot past Jordan Pickford at his near post. For the next hour, DR Congo's goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi delivered the performance of his life — denying Jude Bellingham on multiple occasions, clawing the ball off the line, and making the Three Lions look ordinary.

Then Thomas Tuchel made the call that saved England's World Cup. Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka replaced Noni Madueke and Marcus Rashford just after the hour mark. The impact was immediate.

## Kane's Moment


![Chancel Mbemba — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/24BBRW_-_53535940590_%28cropped%29.jpg)


In the 75th minute, Gordon clipped a ball from the left side. Harry Kane, England's captain, had drifted behind his marker. He met the cross with a glancing header across goal. Mpasi got a hand to it. It wasn't enough. The ball nestled in the corner — 1-1.

Eleven minutes later, Kane wrote himself into history. Bellingham's shot was saved by Mpasi, but England kept the ball alive. Gordon drifted inside, beat two defenders, and found his captain just outside the penalty area. Kane steadied himself, turned, and unleashed a ferocious right-footed strike into the roof of the net. The stadium erupted.



> **"Diego Maradona's "Hand of God" against England happened at the Azteca in 1986."**


That goal — his 13th in World Cup football — moved Kane past Pelé in the all-time World Cup scoring charts. He now sits joint-sixth alongside Germany's Gerd Müller and France's Just Fontaine, behind only Miroslav Klose (16), Ronaldo (15), and Müller's namesake Thomas Müller (14).


![Jordan Pickford — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cc/Jordan_Pickford_England_v_Ghana_23_June_2026-049.jpg)


## What the Numbers Say

Kane's World Cup record is now staggering: 13 goals across three tournaments (2018, 2022, and 2026), with five in this tournament alone — the Golden Boot race is his to lose. He has also overtaken 20 goals at major tournaments overall, and his 84 goals in 118 international caps cement him as England's greatest-ever goalscorer by a wide margin.

For DR Congo, the elimination is heartbreaking but historic. Their first World Cup since 1974 — and only their second ever — produced their first-ever World Cup victory in the group stage and their first knockout-round appearance. The Leopards leave with their heads high.


![Lionel Mpasi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1d/Lionel_Mpasi_%28cropped%29.jpg)


## The Azteca Awaits

England's reward is a Round of 16 date with co-hosts Mexico at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City on Saturday. Mexico are unbeaten in 10 World Cup matches at the iconic 80,000-seat stadium — a ground where altitude, noise, and history conspire against visiting teams. Diego Maradona's "Hand of God" against England happened at the Azteca in 1986. The ghosts of that night will add another layer to what promises to be the tie of the round.

Mexico qualified by topping their group and dispatching Ecuador 2-0 in the Round of 32. They have conceded just one goal in the tournament.

## The Bigger Picture

While the Round of 32 wraps up — Belgium and Senegal went to extra time in Seattle, and the USA face Bosnia and Herzegovina at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara tonight — the Round of 16 bracket is taking shape. France face Paraguay in Philadelphia. Brazil meet Norway at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Canada take on Morocco in Houston.

For the millions of football fans in the Indian diaspora watching from living rooms and sports bars across America, the World Cup being on home soil has made the beautiful game feel closer than ever. Kane's heroics in Atlanta, Mbappé's brace against Sweden in New Jersey, and the drama in Seattle — this tournament is delivering.

*England play Mexico in the Round of 16 on Saturday, July 5, at 1:00 PM PT (4:00 PM ET) at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. The match will be broadcast on FOX.*
